message.reasoning:
Rear view is viewed from wire-entry side, opposite the front mating face. Key at top in both. When viewed from rear, left-right is mirrored relative to front. So rear top-left corresponds to front top-right = pin 4.

Rear layout: top row W Q T P, bottom row U R S V. Rear viewed from back: rear left column maps to front right column. So rear position (top-left, W) = front pin 4; rear top row left-to-right = front pins 4,3,2,1. Rear bottom row = front pins 8,7,6,5.

So mapping: pin1=P, pin2=T, pin3=Q, pin4=W, pin5=V, pin6=S, pin7=R, pin8=U.

TX=pin2 → T; RX=pin7 → R; GND=pin5 → V. rear_top_left_pin = 4.
